The company plans ongoing updates to improve ChatGPT's personality, creativity, and user experience while expanding user choice and maintaining appropriate safeguards.

item.title: Taisei Corporation rolls out ChatGPT Enterprise to enhance talent development with AI across its workforce [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Taisei Corporation, a leading Japanese construction company, has implemented ChatGPT Enterprise as a central part of its talent development strategy, focusing on expanding employee potential through AI rather than just improving productivity. The HR team led the rollout using a "Middle Out" approach that combines leadership direction with frontline engagement, supported by training programs, internal events, and governance measures to ensure safe and confident AI use. Since the rollout, Taisei has seen high adoption rates, significant time savings per employee, and thousands of custom GPTs created, reflecting meaningful changes in how employees work with AI. The company aims to foster a culture where AI use is integrated into daily work and plans to share its human-centered AI model with the broader construction industry and society.

item.title: OpenAI launches €500,000 EMEA Youth & Wellbeing Grant to fund NGOs and researchers focused on AI's impact on youth safety and wellbeing [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced the EMEA Youth & Wellbeing Grant, a €500,000 funding program aimed at supporting NGOs and research organizations working to improve youth safety, wellbeing, and development in the context of artificial intelligence across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. The grant targets projects that produce practical tools, independent research, or initiatives that help young people benefit safely from AI. The program offers grants typically ranging from €25,000 to €100,000, with multi-year awards possible for larger efforts. Eligible applicants must be operational NGOs or research institutions registered in the EMEA region, focusing on youth safety or AI impacts on minors. Applications for 2026 have closed, and finalists have been selected, with projects expected to begin in the second or third quarter of 2026.

item.title: OpenAI launches EU Economic Blueprint 2.0 with new AI adoption data, SME training program, and youth safety grant to boost AI use across Europe [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced the EU Economic Blueprint 2.0, featuring updated data on AI usage in Europe and initiatives to accelerate AI adoption among individuals, businesses, and governments. The plan includes a program to train 20,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in AI skills, supported by Booking.com, and a €500,000 grant to support research on youth safety and wellbeing in the digital age. The Blueprint highlights disparities in AI usage across EU member states and emphasizes the need for national AI strategies, education frameworks, and skills accreditation to close the capability gap. OpenAI also plans to expand partnerships with European governments through its OpenAI for Europe initiative, focusing on education, health, and AI skills training to support national AI priorities.

item.title: OpenAI implements safeguards to prevent data leaks when AI agents fetch URLs by verifying links against a public web index [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced measures to protect user data when AI agents interact with web links, addressing risks of data exfiltration through URLs and prompt injection attacks. The system checks whether a URL has been previously observed on the public web before allowing automatic fetching, reducing the chance of leaking private information. This approach avoids relying solely on trusted site lists, which can be bypassed through redirects or cause user friction. When a URL is unverified, users receive warnings and must explicitly approve access, maintaining control over potentially sensitive data exposure. These safeguards focus on preventing quiet data leaks via URLs but do not guarantee the trustworthiness of web content or protection against social engineering.

item.title: PVH Corp adopts ChatGPT Enterprise to integrate AI across fashion design, supply chain, and consumer engagement for Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: PVH Corp, the parent company of Calvin Klein and Tommy Hilfiger, announced it will use ChatGPT Enterprise to embed AI throughout its global operations, aiming to enhance creativity, efficiency, and data-driven decision-making in fashion design, planning, and consumer engagement. The company plans to apply AI to product creation, demand forecasting, inventory management, and personalized marketing while maintaining strong data security and governance standards. PVH will develop custom AI capabilities combining OpenAI's models with its expertise in fashion and supply chain management to support its long-term growth strategy, the PVH+ Plan. This collaboration seeks to transform the fashion industry by integrating advanced AI with human creativity to improve brand-building and operational agility at scale.

item.title: OpenAI launches Prism, a free LaTeX-native workspace with GPT-5.2 integration for scientific writing and collaboration [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced Prism, a free, AI-native workspace designed to streamline scientific writing and collaboration by integrating GPT-5.2 directly into a LaTeX-based environment. Prism allows researchers to draft, revise, and manage papers with real-time collaboration and AI-assisted reasoning, equations, citations, and literature search all in one cloud-based platform. Built on the foundation of the acquired Crixet platform, Prism supports unlimited collaborators without seat limits or local software installation, aiming to reduce manual overhead and improve workflow efficiency. It is available now to anyone with a ChatGPT personal account, with plans to extend access to organizational ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and Education users.

item.title: TRUSTBANK launches Choice AI using OpenAI models to personalize Furusato Nozei gift recommendations in Japan [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: TRUSTBANK partnered with Recursive to develop Choice AI, an AI-powered feature that simplifies the discovery of thank-you gifts in Japan's Furusato Nozei hometown tax donation program. The system uses OpenAI's GPT-4.1 series models and a multiagent architecture to provide personalized conversational recommendations based on user preferences and donation intent. Furusato Nozei allows taxpayers to support rural municipalities by donating a portion of their taxes in exchange for local specialty gifts, but navigating the extensive catalog of options has been challenging. TRUSTBANK's Choice AI addresses this by dynamically routing user queries to specialized agents that tailor recommendations, improving the user experience especially for first-time donors and helping them make informed decisions within their donation limits.

item.title: Indeed uses AI to enhance job search and recruiting with new features like Career Scout and Talent Scout, aiming to improve matching and efficiency for employers and job seekers [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Indeed's Chief Revenue Officer Maggie Hulce discusses how the company integrates AI across its platform to simplify and speed up hiring processes for both job seekers and employers. The platform employs over a hundred AI-powered features, including personalized job recommendations and candidate matching, developed in collaboration with OpenAI. Recent launches include AI agents Career Scout and Talent Scout, designed to assist job seekers and recruiters respectively. Indeed emphasizes responsible AI use, ensuring employers remain the final decision-makers. Internally, AI adoption has increased productivity by automating repetitive tasks, allowing teams to focus on strategic work. The company supports AI fluency through training programs, internal sharing, and incentives to foster innovation and confidence among employees.

item.title: OpenAI details Codex CLI agent loop orchestrating models, tools, and prompts for software tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI explains the core agent loop in Codex CLI, which manages interactions between users, language models, and tools to perform software changes efficiently and safely on local machines. The loop involves generating prompts, querying models, executing tool calls, and iterating until a final user response or action is produced. The article outlines how Codex CLI handles tokenization, inference, and context window management to maintain conversation history and tool execution within model limits. It also highlights that the agent's output includes both assistant messages and code modifications on the user's machine, marking the completion of each interaction cycle.

item.title: OpenAI scales PostgreSQL to support 800 million ChatGPT users with millions of queries per second using replicas, caching, and workload isolation [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has scaled its PostgreSQL database to handle the demands of 800 million ChatGPT users by supporting millions of queries per second through a single primary instance and nearly 50 read replicas globally. The company optimized its infrastructure with caching, rate limiting, and workload isolation to manage rapid growth and maintain performance. Despite PostgreSQL's limitations with write-heavy workloads due to its multiversion concurrency control, OpenAI mitigated write pressure by migrating write-heavy workloads to sharded systems like Azure Cosmos DB and restricting new tables on PostgreSQL. The single-primary architecture remains effective for their read-heavy workloads, providing sufficient capacity for ongoing growth without immediate plans for sharding PostgreSQL.

item.title: Praktika uses GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.2 to power adaptive AI tutors that personalize language lessons and track learner progress for real-world fluency [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Praktika has developed a language learning app that employs GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.2 to create AI tutors capable of adapting lessons based on individual learner behavior, goals, and conversation context. The system includes multiple AI agents that simulate real tutors by monitoring progress, adjusting lesson plans, and responding dynamically during conversations to improve fluency and confidence. The app's multi-agent architecture features a Lesson Agent for interactive tutoring, a Student Progress Agent that tracks language performance, and a Learning Planning Agent that personalizes long-term learning strategies. Praktika's approach emphasizes real-time memory retrieval and advanced speech recognition to make AI conversations feel natural and responsive, helping users bridge the gap between classroom learning and practical language use in work and daily life.

item.title: OpenAI publishes data-driven report on ChatGPT usage and adoption patterns across industries and departments at work [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI released a report analyzing how ChatGPT is used by workers across various industries and job functions, highlighting adoption trends, common tasks, and departmental usage patterns. The report draws on anonymized usage data combined with independent studies to provide insights into AI integration in the workplace. The analysis shows rapid adoption of ChatGPT since its 2022 launch, with over a quarter of U.S. workers using it for work-related tasks. Industries like IT, finance, and manufacturing lead in adoption, while sectors such as retail and healthcare show slower uptake due to factors like compliance and workforce composition. Early usage focuses on writing, research, programming, and analysis, reflecting ChatGPT's versatility in supporting core workflows.

item.title: OpenAI Blog: Higgsfield uses GPT-4.1, GPT-5, and Sora 2 to generate 4 million cinematic social videos daily from simple inputs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Higgsfield is a generative media platform that transforms simple inputs like product links or images into short-form, cinematic social videos using OpenAI's GPT-4.1, GPT-5 for planning, and Sora 2 for video creation. The system generates about 4 million videos per day, applying a cinematic logic layer to interpret creative intent and produce structured, trend-aligned content without requiring users to provide technical video instructions. The platform operationalizes virality by analyzing social video patterns to create and update a library of video presets that guide pacing, narrative, and camera logic, resulting in a 150% increase in share velocity and triple cognitive capture compared to earlier methods. Features like Click-to-Ad enable users to generate social-ready ads from product pages quickly, supporting high-volume, trend-responsive video production for marketing teams.

item.title: OpenAI outlines global AI adoption gaps and launches initiatives to help countries boost productivity through advanced AI use in education, health, and public services [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI's new report highlights significant disparities in advanced AI adoption across more than 70 countries, revealing that some nations use AI's complex capabilities up to three times more per person than others, regardless of income levels. This capability overhang risks widening economic and technological divides as countries that adopt AI more deeply gain productivity and innovation advantages. To address this, OpenAI is expanding its OpenAI for Countries program in 2026 with initiatives focused on integrating AI into education, health, disaster response, cybersecurity, and startup support. The program partners with governments to tailor AI adoption strategies that improve workforce skills, public services, and institutional strength, aiming to help more countries capture AI-driven economic growth and prepare for future job markets.

item.title: OpenAI launches Education for Countries initiative to help governments integrate AI into education systems and workforce training [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has introduced Education for Countries, a new initiative aimed at assisting governments in modernizing education systems by embedding AI tools, training, and research to prepare students for future workforce demands. The program collaborates with ministries, universities, and researchers to provide AI-powered learning tools, conduct large-scale research on AI's impact in education, and offer certifications aligned with national workforce priorities. The initiative's first cohort includes Estonia, Greece, Italy, Jordan, Kazakhstan, Slovakia, Trinidad & Tobago, and the United Arab Emirates, with deployments such as Estonia's nationwide use of ChatGPT Edu reaching over 30,000 users. OpenAI emphasizes a phased rollout focusing on educator training and pilot programs for students, alongside efforts to ensure AI safety and literacy for young users. This program aligns with OpenAI's mission to expand economic opportunity and ensure AI benefits are broadly accessible.

item.title: OpenAI and Gates Foundation launch $50M Horizon 1000 pilot to advance AI in 1,000 African primary healthcare clinics by 2028 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI and the Gates Foundation have announced Horizon 1000, a $50 million initiative to support the deployment of AI technologies in primary healthcare across 1,000 clinics in Africa by 2028. The program aims to strengthen healthcare delivery by providing funding, technology, and technical support, starting with Rwanda. The initiative addresses the shortage of healthcare workers and variable quality of care in Sub-Saharan Africa by helping frontline health workers use AI tools to navigate complex guidelines and reduce administrative burdens. Horizon 1000 seeks to improve patient care and support health workers while promoting African leadership in healthcare innovation.

item.title: OpenAI outlines Stargate Community plans to tailor AI infrastructure development with local input, energy commitments, and workforce priorities across US sites [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI is advancing its Stargate AI infrastructure initiative with a community-first approach that emphasizes local input, energy responsibility, and economic benefits. The company aims to expand its U.S. AI capacity to 10GW by 2029, with several sites already operational or in development across Texas, New Mexico, Wisconsin, and Michigan. Each Stargate site will have a customized community plan addressing local energy needs and grid conditions, including commitments to fund energy generation and grid upgrades without raising local electricity prices. Partnerships with utilities and developers are underway to implement these plans, such as solar and battery storage projects in Wisconsin and Michigan, and new energy generation in Texas. OpenAI also prioritizes minimizing water use and protecting ecosystems through advanced cooling technologies.

item.title: ServiceNow expands access to OpenAI models to power AI-driven enterprise workflows and voice capabilities across its platform [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: ServiceNow announced a multi-year agreement to integrate OpenAI's frontier models, including GPT-5.2, as a preferred intelligence capability for enterprises running over 80 billion workflows annually on its platform. This integration enables AI to understand, decide, and act within enterprise workflows securely, enhancing automation across IT, finance, sales, and human resources functions. The partnership supports AI-powered features such as natural language assistance, summarization, content generation, intelligent search, and developer tools that convert intent into automated workflows. ServiceNow and OpenAI aim to develop more natural, multimodal AI experiences that allow users to interact via speech, text, or visuals, helping enterprises deploy scalable, agentic AI to improve operational efficiency and decision-making.

item.title: OpenAI rolls out age prediction on ChatGPT to identify users under 18 and apply teen-specific safeguards [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI is deploying an age prediction model on ChatGPT consumer plans to estimate whether accounts belong to users under 18, enabling the application of tailored safeguards to protect teens. The model analyzes behavioral and account signals such as activity patterns and stated age, with users able to verify their age via a secure selfie process to regain full access if misclassified. The safeguards reduce exposure to sensitive content including graphic violence, risky viral challenges, sexual or violent role play, self-harm depictions, and harmful body image content. This approach is informed by expert input and child development research, with ongoing efforts to improve accuracy and prevent circumvention. Parental controls also allow customization of teen experiences, including usage limits and distress notifications. The rollout will expand to the EU soon, with OpenAI continuing to refine protections and engage with experts on teen safety.

item.title: OpenAI outlines business model scaling with intelligence value through subscriptions, API usage, ads, commerce, and compute amid growing ChatGPT adoption [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI describes how its business model grows in line with the value delivered by its AI intelligence, particularly through ChatGPT's widespread adoption. The company has expanded from consumer subscriptions to workplace plans, usage-based pricing, and a platform for developers, aligning revenue growth with increasing compute capacity and user engagement. The model integrates commerce and advertising by helping users move from exploration to decision-making, ensuring monetization adds genuine value. OpenAI reports significant growth in compute resources and revenue from 2023 to 2025, emphasizing a diversified compute ecosystem that supports scalable AI services for everyday workflows beyond elite use cases.

item.title: Google DeepMind introduces D4RT for unified 4D reconstruction and tracking, achieving up to 300x speed improvements over prior methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Google DeepMind has developed D4RT, a system that enables AI to perform unified and efficient four-dimensional reconstruction and tracking. This technology significantly accelerates processing speeds, reaching up to 300 times faster than previous approaches. D4RT's advancements could enhance AI perception capabilities in dynamic environments, facilitating more responsive and accurate spatial understanding.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Go worldwide with GPT-5.2 Instant access, higher usage limits, and longer memory at $8 per month in the US [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has expanded ChatGPT Go, a low-cost subscription plan offering access to its GPT-5.2 Instant model, to all countries where ChatGPT is available. Originally launched in India in August 2025, ChatGPT Go provides users with increased message limits, file uploads, image creation, and longer memory compared to the free tier, aiming to make advanced AI more affordable globally. ChatGPT Go joins OpenAI's subscription lineup alongside ChatGPT Plus and ChatGPT Pro, which offer progressively higher capabilities and pricing. The company plans to introduce ads in the free tier and ChatGPT Go in the US to support accessibility, while paid tiers will remain ad-free.

item.title: OpenAI plans to test ads in the U.S. on ChatGPT free and Go tiers to expand affordable AI access while preserving privacy and answer quality [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI announced plans to introduce advertising on the free and ChatGPT Go subscription tiers in the U.S. to support broader access to AI tools. The company emphasized that ads will be clearly labeled, separate from ChatGPT's responses, and will not influence the answers provided, maintaining user trust and privacy. ChatGPT Go, a low-cost subscription offering expanded features, is now available in the U.S. alongside the free tier. OpenAI will not include ads in Pro, Business, or Enterprise subscriptions and will exclude ads from accounts of users under 18 or near sensitive topics. The company highlighted principles guiding its ad approach, including mission alignment, answer independence, conversation privacy, user control over data, and prioritizing long-term user trust over revenue. OpenAI plans to start testing ads in the coming weeks, gathering user feedback to refine the experience. The initiative aims to create a diverse revenue model that supports affordable AI access globally while maintaining the quality and trustworthiness of ChatGPT's services.

item.title: OpenAI invests in Merge Labs to develop high-bandwidth brain-computer interfaces combining biology and AI [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI is investing in Merge Labs to advance brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) that integrate biological and artificial intelligence to enhance human ability and interaction with technology. Merge Labs aims to create safe, high-bandwidth BCIs by combining bioengineering, neuroscience, device engineering, and AI. OpenAI will collaborate with Merge Labs on scientific foundation models and AI tools to accelerate research and development. Merge Labs' co-founders include researchers Mikhail Shapiro, Tyson Aflalo, and Sumner Norman, supported by technology entrepreneurs including Sam Altman in a personal capacity.

item.title: OpenAI launches RFP to boost U.S. AI supply chain by expanding domestic manufacturing of data center hardware, consumer electronics, and robotics components [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has issued a new Request for Proposals aimed at strengthening the U.S. AI supply chain by accelerating domestic manufacturing of critical components for data centers, consumer electronics, and robotics. This initiative supports the company's broader Stargate effort to build AI infrastructure capacity and create well-paid jobs across the country. The RFP seeks manufacturers and suppliers capable of producing modules, tooling, assembly equipment, and key inputs like power electronics and cooling systems within the United States. OpenAI plans to use responses to guide partnerships and procurement strategies that enhance supply chain resilience and maintain American leadership in AI technology as infrastructure scales. This effort is part of a wider push toward reindustrialization, with manufacturers investing in advanced production capabilities and workforce expansion to ensure AI benefits are developed and shared domestically. The deadline for proposal submissions is June 2026, with reviews conducted on a rolling basis.

item.title: OpenAI partners with Cerebras to add 750MW of low-latency AI compute for faster real-time inference, with capacity rolling out through 2028 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI has partnered with Cerebras to integrate 750MW of ultra low-latency AI compute into its platform, aiming to reduce inference latency and speed up responses for real-time AI workloads such as code generation, image creation, and AI agents. Cerebras' technology combines massive compute, memory, and bandwidth on a single chip to eliminate bottlenecks that slow AI inference on conventional hardware. The integration will occur in phases through 2028, enhancing OpenAI's inference stack to support faster, more natural AI interactions and enabling the scaling of real-time AI to more users. OpenAI describes this partnership as part of its strategy to match the right compute systems to specific workloads, while Cerebras highlights the potential for real-time inference to transform AI usage similarly to how broadband transformed the internet.

item.title: Google DeepMind updates Veo 3.1 to generate more expressive, consistent videos with vertical format support and upscaling to 1080p and 4K [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Google DeepMind has released Veo 3.1, an update to its Ingredients to Video tool that enhances video expressiveness, character and background consistency, and supports native vertical video output for platforms like YouTube Shorts. The update also introduces upscaling options to 1080p and 4K resolution, enabling higher-fidelity video production directly from images on mobile devices. Veo 3.1 improvements include richer dialogue and storytelling from simple prompts, better identity consistency for characters across scenes, and the ability to maintain consistent backgrounds and objects. These features allow creators to produce cohesive, dynamic clips with seamless blending of textures and elements. The update is available across multiple platforms including the Gemini app, YouTube Shorts, Flow, Google Vids, the Gemini API, and Vertex AI, catering to both casual users and professional filmmakers.

item.title: Zenken adopts ChatGPT Enterprise to enhance sales efficiency and proposal success, achieving over 90% weekly usage and significant time savings [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Zenken has implemented ChatGPT Enterprise across its organization to improve sales performance, reduce preparation time, and increase proposal approval rates. The company reports more than 90% weekly active usage, 30 to 50% time savings on knowledge tasks, and reinvestment of saved hours into higher-value work, leading to a 5 to 10% increase in new deal win rates and a 30% rise in final proposal approvals. Zenken chose ChatGPT Enterprise for its security features and advanced reasoning models, which support complex business analysis and strategic decision-making. The AI tools have transformed sales workflows by enabling deeper industry analysis, real-time responses during meetings, and personalized proposals, helping the lean sales team engage customers more effectively and reduce outsourcing costs by 50 million yen annually.

item.title: OpenAI and SoftBank Group invest $1 billion in SB Energy to develop multi-gigawatt AI data center campuses including a 1.2 GW Texas facility under the Stargate initiative [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI and SoftBank Group have each invested $500 million in SB Energy to support the development of large-scale AI data center campuses, including a 1.2 gigawatt facility in Milam County, Texas. This partnership is part of the broader Stargate initiative aimed at advancing AI and energy infrastructure in the United States. SB Energy will build and operate the Texas data center, which is expected to begin service in 2026 and create thousands of construction jobs. The collaboration combines OpenAI's data center engineering expertise with SB Energy's infrastructure and energy development capabilities, focusing on efficient, purpose-built AI infrastructure with attention to water usage and energy needs to benefit local communities and ratepayers.

item.title: Datadog integrates OpenAI Codex for system-level code review to identify risks beyond traditional tools, improving incident prevention across its engineering teams [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Datadog has adopted OpenAI's Codex to enhance its code review process by incorporating system-wide context, enabling the detection of risks that traditional static analysis tools often miss. This integration aims to prevent incidents and maintain customer trust by providing deeper insights into how code changes affect interconnected systems. The company piloted Codex in one of its largest repositories, automatically reviewing every pull request and gathering engineer feedback that highlighted Codex's valuable and relevant suggestions. Datadog validated Codex's effectiveness by replaying historical incidents, finding that it identified potential issues in about 22% of cases that human reviewers had overlooked. The tool's ability to reason over the entire codebase and dependencies has led to broader deployment among over 1,000 engineers, who report that Codex's feedback feels like input from a highly knowledgeable engineer with extensive time to find bugs.

item.title: OpenAI launches OpenAI for Healthcare with HIPAA-compliant AI tools including ChatGPT for Healthcare, partnering with major US health systems starting January 2026 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduced OpenAI for Healthcare, a suite of secure AI products designed to help healthcare organizations improve care quality, reduce administrative workload, and maintain HIPAA compliance. The offering includes ChatGPT for Healthcare, which supports clinical, research, and operational workflows with evidence-based responses and institutional policy integration, and is already deployed at leading institutions such as AdventHealth and UCSF. The platform features role-based access controls, data residency options, audit logs, and a Business Associate Agreement to ensure patient data protection and compliance. It aims to address the growing strain on healthcare by enabling clinicians to synthesize medical evidence, automate documentation, and follow consistent care pathways while keeping clinicians in control of patient care decisions.

item.title: Netomi scales enterprise AI agents using GPT-4.1 and GPT-5.2 with concurrency and governance for reliable multi-step workflows [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Netomi has developed a platform that uses OpenAI's GPT-4.1 for fast, reliable tool use and GPT-5.2 for deeper multi-step planning to scale AI agents across complex enterprise workflows. The system is designed to handle real-world ambiguity, maintain policy compliance, and operate under heavy load for Fortune 500 clients like United Airlines and DraftKings. The platform employs a governed orchestration pipeline that supports concurrency to meet enterprise latency expectations, enabling sub-three-second responses even during traffic spikes exceeding 40,000 concurrent requests per second. Netomi's approach includes persistence reminders, explicit tool-use expectations, and structured planning to ensure consistent agent behavior across long, multi-step tasks, addressing challenges in industries such as airlines where workflows span multiple systems and policies.

item.title: How Tolan builds voice-first AI with GPT-5.1 [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Tolan built a voice-first AI companion with GPT-5.1, combining low-latency responses, real-time context reconstruction, and memory-driven personalities for natural conversations.

item.description: ChatGPT Health is a dedicated experience that securely connects your health data and apps, with privacy protections and a physician-informed design.

item.description: Applications are now open for OpenAI Grove Cohort 2, a 5-week founder program designed for individuals at any stage, from pre-idea to product. Participants receive $50K in API credits, early access to AI tools, and hands-on mentorship from the OpenAI team.

item.description: OpenAI is strengthening ChatGPT Atlas against prompt injection attacks using automated red teaming trained with reinforcement learning. This proactive discover-and-patch loop helps identify novel exploits early and harden the browser agent's defenses as AI becomes more agentic.

item.title: One in a million: celebrating the customers shaping AI's future [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: More than one million customers around the world now use OpenAI to empower their teams and unlock new opportunities. This post highlights how companies like PayPal, Virgin Atlantic, BBVA, Cisco, Moderna, and Canva are transforming the way work gets done with AI.

item.title: Evaluating chain-of-thought monitorability [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI introduces a new framework and evaluation suite for chain-of-thought monitorability, covering 13 evaluations across 24 environments. Our findings show that monitoring a model's internal reasoning is far more effective than monitoring outputs alone, offering a promising path toward scalable control as AI systems grow more capable.

item.title: Deepening our collaboration with the U.S. Department of Energy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: OpenAI and the U.S. Department of Energy have signed a memorandum of understanding to deepen collaboration on AI and advanced computing in support of scientific discovery. The agreement builds on ongoing work with national laboratories and helps establish a framework for applying AI to high-impact research across the DOE ecosystem.

item.title: Updating our Model Spec with teen protections [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI is updating its Model Spec with new Under-18 Principles that define how ChatGPT should support teens with safe, age-appropriate guidance grounded in developmental science. item.title: Video generation models as world simulators
item.description: We explore large-scale training of generative models on video data. Specifically, we train text-conditional diffusion models jointly on videos and images of variable durations, resolutions and aspect ratios. We leverage a transformer architecture that operates on spacetime patches of video and image latent codes. Our largest model, Sora, is capable of generating a minute of high fidelity video. Our results suggest that scaling video generation models is a promising path towards building general purpose simulators of the physical world.

item.title: Building an early warning system for LLM-aided biological threat creation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers are developing a framework to assess the potential risk of large language models (LLMs) like GPT-4 being used to assist in creating biological threats. An evaluation involving biology experts and students indicated that GPT-4 offers only a slight improvement in accuracy for biological threat creation, which is not significant enough to draw definitive conclusions. This work serves as an initial step for ongoing research and discussions within the community.

item.title: Forecasting potential misuses of language models for disinformation campaigns and how to reduce risk
item.description: OpenAI researchers collaborated with Georgetown University's Center for Security and Emerging Technology and the Stanford Internet Observatory to investigate how large language models might be misused for disinformation purposes. The collaboration included an October 2021 workshop bringing together 30 disinformation researchers, machine learning experts, and policy analysts, and culminated in a co-authored report building on more than a year of research. This report outlines the threats that language models pose to the information environment if used to augment disinformation campaigns and introduces a framework for analyzing potential mitigations. Read the full report here.

item.title: Learning to play Minecraft with Video PreTraining
item.description: We trained a neural network to play Minecraft by Video PreTraining (VPT) on a massive unlabeled video dataset of human Minecraft play, while using only a small amount of labeled contractor data. With fine-tuning, our model can learn to craft diamond tools, a task that usually takes proficient humans over 20 minutes (24,000 actions). Our model uses the native human interface of keypresses and mouse movements, making it quite general, and represents a step towards general computer-using agents.

item.title: Evolution through large models
AI-written critiques help humans notice flaws
item.description: We trained "critique-writing" models to describe flaws in summaries. Human evaluators find flaws in summaries much more often when shown our model's critiques. Larger models are better at self-critiquing, with scale improving critique-writing more than summary-writing. This shows promise for using AI systems to assist human supervision of AI systems on difficult tasks.

item.title: Image GPT
item.description: We find that, just as a large transformer model trained on language can generate coherent text, the same exact model trained on pixel sequences can generate coherent image completions and samples. By establishing a correlation between sample quality and image classification accuracy, we show that our best generative model also contains features competitive with top convolutional nets in the unsupervised setting.

item.title: Language models are few-shot learners
AI and efficiency
item.description: We're releasing an analysis showing that since 2012 the amount of compute needed to train a neural net to the same performance on ImageNet classification has been decreasing by a factor of 2 every 16 months. Compared to 2012, it now takes 44 times less compute to train a neural network to the level of AlexNet (by contrast, Moore's Law would yield an 11x cost improvement over this period). Our results suggest that for AI tasks with high levels of recent investment, algorithmic progress has yielded more gains than classical hardware efficiency.

item.title: Jukebox
item.description: We're introducing Jukebox, a neural net that generates music, including rudimentary singing, as raw audio in a variety of genres and artist styles. We're releasing the model weights and code, along with a tool to explore the generated samples.

item.title: Improving verifiability in AI development
item.description: We've contributed to a multi-stakeholder report by 58 co-authors at 30 organizations, including the Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Mila, Schwartz Reisman Institute for Technology and Society, Center for Advanced Study in the Behavioral Sciences, and Center for Security and Emerging Technologies. This report describes 10 mechanisms to improve the verifiability of claims made about AI systems. Developers can use these tools to provide evidence that AI systems are safe, secure, fair, or privacy-preserving. Users, policymakers, and civil society can use these tools to evaluate AI development processes.

item.title: OpenAI Microscope
item.description: We're introducing OpenAI Microscope, a collection of visualizations of every significant layer and neuron of eight vision "model organisms" which are often studied in interpretability. Microscope makes it easier to analyze the features that form inside these neural networks, and we hope it will help the research community as we move towards understanding these complicated systems.

item.title: OpenAI standardizes on PyTorch
item.description: We are standardizing OpenAI's deep learning framework on PyTorch.

item.title: Scaling laws for neural language models
Dota 2 with large scale deep reinforcement learning
Deep double descent
item.description: We show that the double descent phenomenon occurs in CNNs, ResNets, and transformers: performance first improves, then gets worse, and then improves again with increasing model size, data size, or training time. This effect is often avoided through careful regularization. While this behavior appears to be fairly universal, we don't yet fully understand why it happens, and view further study of this phenomenon as an important research direction.

item.title: Procgen Benchmark
item.description: We're releasing Procgen Benchmark, 16 simple-to-use procedurally-generated environments which provide a direct measure of how quickly a reinforcement learning agent learns generalizable skills.

item.title: Safety Gym
item.description: We're releasing Safety Gym, a suite of environments and tools for measuring progress towards reinforcement learning agents that respect safety constraints while training.

item.title: Benchmarking safe exploration in deep reinforcement learning
GPT-2: 1.5B release
item.description: As the final model release of GPT-2's staged release, we're releasing the largest version (1.5B parameters) of GPT-2 along with code and model weights to facilitate detection of outputs of GPT-2 models. While there have been larger language models released since August, we've continued with our original staged release plan in order to provide the community with a test case of a full staged release process. We hope that this test case will be useful to developers of future powerful models, and we're actively continuing the conversation with the AI community on responsible publication.

item.title: Solving Rubik's Cube with a robot hand
item.description: We've trained a pair of neural networks to solve the Rubik's Cube with a human-like robot hand. The neural networks are trained entirely in simulation, using the same reinforcement learning code as OpenAI Five paired with a new technique called Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR). The system can handle situations it never saw during training, such as being prodded by a stuffed giraffe. This shows that reinforcement learning isn't just a tool for virtual tasks, but can solve physical-world problems requiring unprecedented dexterity.

item.title: OpenAI Scholars 2020: Applications open
item.description: We are now accepting applications for our third class of OpenAI Scholars.

item.title: Fine-tuning GPT-2 from human preferences
item.description: We've fine-tuned the 774M parameter GPT-2 language model using human feedback for various tasks, successfully matching the preferences of the external human labelers, though those preferences did not always match our own. Specifically, for summarization tasks the labelers preferred sentences copied wholesale from the input (we'd only asked them to ensure accuracy), so our models learned to copy. Summarization required 60k human labels; simpler tasks which continue text in various styles required only 5k. Our motivation is to move safety techniques closer to the general task of "machines talking to humans," which we believe is key to extracting information about human values.

item.title: Emergent tool use from multi-agent interaction
item.description: We've observed agents discovering progressively more complex tool use while playing a simple game of hide-and-seek. Through training in our new simulated hide-and-seek environment, agents build a series of six distinct strategies and counterstrategies, some of which we did not know our environment supported. The self-supervised emergent complexity in this simple environment further suggests that multi-agent co-adaptation may one day produce extremely complex and intelligent behavior.

item.title: Testing robustness against unforeseen adversaries
item.description: We've developed a method to assess whether a neural network classifier can reliably defend against adversarial attacks not seen during training. Our method yields a new metric, UAR (Unforeseen Attack Robustness), which evaluates the robustness of a single model against an unanticipated attack, and highlights the need to measure performance across a more diverse range of unforeseen attacks.

item.title: GPT-2: 6-month follow-up
item.description: We're releasing the 774 million parameter GPT-2 language model after the release of our small 124M model in February, staged release of our medium 355M model in May, and subsequent research with partners and the AI community into the model's potential for misuse and societal benefit. We're also releasing an open-source legal agreement to make it easier for organizations to initiate model-sharing partnerships with each other, and are publishing a technical report about our experience in coordinating with the wider AI research community on publication norms.

item.title: Learning Day
item.description: At OpenAI, each Thursday is Learning Day: a day where employees have the option to self-study technical skills that will make them better at their job but which aren't being learned from daily work.

item.title: Microsoft invests in and partners with OpenAI to support us building beneficial AGI
item.description: Microsoft is investing $1 billion in OpenAI to support us building artificial general intelligence (AGI) with widely distributed economic benefits. We're partnering to develop a hardware and software platform within Microsoft Azure which will scale to AGI. We'll jointly develop new Azure AI supercomputing technologies, and Microsoft will become our exclusive cloud provider-so we'll be working hard together to further extend Microsoft Azure's capabilities in large-scale AI systems.

item.title: Why responsible AI development needs cooperation on safety
item.description: We've written a policy research paper identifying four strategies that can be used today to improve the likelihood of long-term industry cooperation on safety norms in AI: communicating risks and benefits, technical collaboration, increased transparency, and incentivizing standards. Our analysis shows that industry cooperation on safety will be instrumental in ensuring that AI systems are safe and beneficial, but competitive pressures could lead to a collective action problem, potentially causing AI companies to under-invest in safety. We hope these strategies will encourage greater cooperation on the safe development of AI and lead to better global outcomes of AI.

item.title: OpenAI Robotics Symposium 2019
item.description: We hosted the first OpenAI Robotics Symposium on April 27, 2019.

item.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Final projects
item.description: Our second class of OpenAI Scholars has concluded, with all eight scholars producing an exciting final project showcased at Scholars Demo Day at OpenAI.

item.title: OpenAI Fellows Fall 2018: Final projects
item.description: Our second class of OpenAI Fellows has wrapped up, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship. We are currently reviewing applications on a rolling basis for our next round of OpenAI Fellows Summer 2019.

item.title: Transfer of adversarial robustness between perturbation types
MuseNet
item.description: We've created MuseNet, a deep neural network that can generate 4-minute musical compositions with 10 different instruments, and can combine styles from country to Mozart to the Beatles. MuseNet was not explicitly programmed with our understanding of music, but instead discovered patterns of harmony, rhythm, and style by learning to predict the next token in hundreds of thousands of MIDI files. MuseNet uses the same general-purpose unsupervised technology as GPT-2, a large-scale transformer model trained to predict the next token in a sequence, whether audio or text.

item.title: Generative modeling with sparse transformers
item.description: We've developed the Sparse Transformer, a deep neural network which sets new records at predicting what comes next in a sequence-whether text, images, or sound. It uses an algorithmic improvement of the attention mechanism to extract patterns from sequences 30x longer than possible previously.

item.title: OpenAI Five defeats Dota 2 world champions
item.description: OpenAI Five is the first AI to beat the world champions in an esports game, having won two back-to-back games versus the world champion Dota 2 team, OG, at Finals this weekend. Both OpenAI Five and DeepMind's AlphaStar had previously beaten good pros privately but lost their live pro matches, making this also the first time an AI has beaten esports pros on livestream.

item.title: OpenAI Five Finals
item.description: We'll be holding our final live event for OpenAI Five at 11:30am PT on April 13.

item.title: Implicit generation and generalization methods for energy-based models
item.description: We've made progress towards stable and scalable training of energy-based models (EBMs) resulting in better sample quality and generalization ability than existing models. Generation in EBMs spends more compute to continually refine its answers and doing so can generate samples competitive with GANs at low temperatures, while also having mode coverage guarantees of likelihood-based models. We hope these findings stimulate further research into this promising class of models.

item.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Meet our Scholars
item.description: Our class of eight scholars (out of 550 applicants) brings together collective expertise in literature, philosophy, cell biology, statistics, economics, quantum physics, and business innovation.

item.title: OpenAI LP
item.description: We've created OpenAI LP, a new "capped-profit" company that allows us to rapidly increase our investments in compute and talent while including checks and balances to actualize our mission.

item.title: Introducing Activation Atlases
item.description: We've created activation atlases (in collaboration with Google researchers), a new technique for visualizing what interactions between neurons can represent. As AI systems are deployed in increasingly sensitive contexts, having a better understanding of their internal decision-making processes will let us identify weaknesses and investigate failures.

item.title: Neural MMO: A massively multiagent game environment
item.description: We're releasing a Neural MMO, a massively multiagent game environment for reinforcement learning agents. Our platform supports a large, variable number of agents within a persistent and open-ended task. The inclusion of many agents and species leads to better exploration, divergent niche formation, and greater overall competence.

item.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL: Workshop review
item.description: On February 2, we held our first Spinning Up Workshop as part of our new education initiative at OpenAI.

item.title: AI safety needs social scientists
item.description: We've written a paper arguing that long-term AI safety research needs social scientists to ensure AI alignment algorithms succeed when actual humans are involved. Properly aligning advanced AI systems with human values requires resolving many uncertainties related to the psychology of human rationality, emotion, and biases. The aim of this paper is to spark further collaboration between machine learning and social science researchers, and we plan to hire social scientists to work on this full time at OpenAI.

item.title: Better language models and their implications
item.description: We've trained a large-scale unsupervised language model which generates coherent paragraphs of text, achieves state-of-the-art performance on many language modeling benchmarks, and performs rudimentary reading comprehension, machine translation, question answering, and summarization-all without task-specific training.

item.title: Computational limitations in robust classification and win-win results
OpenAI Fellows Summer 2018: Final projects
item.description: Our first cohort of OpenAI Fellows has concluded, with each Fellow going from a machine learning beginner to core OpenAI contributor in the course of a 6-month apprenticeship.

item.title: How AI training scales
item.description: We've discovered that the gradient noise scale, a simple statistical metric, predicts the parallelizability of neural network training on a wide range of tasks. Since complex tasks tend to have noisier gradients, increasingly large batch sizes are likely to become useful in the future, removing one potential limit to further growth of AI systems. More broadly, these results show that neural network training need not be considered a mysterious art, but can be rigorized and systematized.

item.title: Quantifying generalization in reinforcement learning
item.description: We're releasing CoinRun, a training environment which provides a metric for an agent's ability to transfer its experience to novel situations and has already helped clarify a longstanding puzzle in reinforcement learning. CoinRun strikes a desirable balance in complexity: the environment is simpler than traditional platformer games like Sonic the Hedgehog but still poses a worthy generalization challenge for state of the art algorithms.

item.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL
item.description: We're releasing Spinning Up in Deep RL, an educational resource designed to let anyone learn to become a skilled practitioner in deep reinforcement learning. Spinning Up consists of crystal-clear examples of RL code, educational exercises, documentation, and tutorials.

item.title: Learning concepts with energy functions
item.description: We've developed an energy-based model that can quickly learn to identify and generate instances of concepts, such as near, above, between, closest, and furthest, expressed as sets of 2d points. Our model learns these concepts after only five demonstrations. We also show cross-domain transfer: we use concepts learned in a 2d particle environment to solve tasks on a 3-dimensional physics-based robot.

item.title: Plan online, learn offline: Efficient learning and exploration via model-based control
Reinforcement learning with prediction-based rewards [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Random Network Distillation (RND), a prediction-based technique designed to motivate reinforcement learning agents to explore their environments by fostering curiosity. This method has achieved performance surpassing the average human level on the challenging game Montezuma's Revenge.

item.title: Learning complex goals with iterated amplification
item.description: We're proposing an AI safety technique called iterated amplification that lets us specify complicated behaviors and goals that are beyond human scale, by demonstrating how to decompose a task into simpler sub-tasks, rather than by providing labeled data or a reward function. Although this idea is in its very early stages and we have only completed experiments on simple toy algorithmic domains, we've decided to present it in its preliminary state because we think it could prove to be a scalable approach to AI safety.

item.title: OpenAI Scholars 2019: Applications open
item.description: We are now accepting applications for our second cohort of OpenAI Scholars, a program where we provide 6-10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.

item.title: OpenAI Fellows Winter 2019 & Interns Summer 2019
item.description: We are now accepting applications for OpenAI Fellows and Interns for 2019.

item.title: FFJORD: Free-form continuous dynamics for scalable reversible generative models
OpenAI Scholars 2018: Final projects
item.description: Our first cohort of OpenAI Scholars has now completed the program.

item.title: The International 2018: Results
item.description: OpenAI Five lost two games against top Dota 2 players at The International in Vancouver this week, maintaining a good chance of winning for the first 20-35 minutes of both games.

item.title: Large-scale study of curiosity-driven learning
OpenAI Five Benchmark: Results
item.description: Yesterday, OpenAI Five won a best-of-three against a team of 99.95th percentile Dota players: Blitz, Cap, Fogged, Merlini, and MoonMeander-four of whom have played Dota professionally-in front of a live audience and 100,000 concurrent livestream viewers.

item.title: Learning dexterity
item.description: We've trained a human-like robot hand to manipulate physical objects with unprecedented dexterity.

item.title: Variational option discovery algorithms
OpenAI Scholars 2018: Meet our Scholars [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Our first class of OpenAI Scholars is underway, and you can now follow along as this group of experienced software developers becomes machine learning practitioners.

item.title: OpenAI Five Benchmark
item.description: The OpenAI Five Benchmark match is now over!

item.title: Glow: Better reversible generative models
item.description: We introduce Glow, a reversible generative model which uses invertible 1x1 convolutions. It extends previous work on reversible generative models and simplifies the architecture. Our model can generate realistic high resolution images, supports efficient sampling, and discovers features that can be used to manipulate attributes of data. We're releasing code for the model and an online visualization tool so people can explore and build on these results.

item.title: Learning Montezuma's Revenge from a single demonstration
item.description: We've trained an agent to achieve a high score of 74,500 on Montezuma's Revenge from a single human demonstration, better than any previously published result. Our algorithm is simple: the agent plays a sequence of games starting from carefully chosen states from the demonstration, and learns from them by optimizing the game score using PPO, the same reinforcement learning algorithm that underpins OpenAI Five.

item.title: OpenAI Five
item.description: Our team of five neural networks, OpenAI Five, has started to defeat amateur human teams at Dota 2.

item.title: Retro Contest: Results
item.description: The first run of our Retro Contest-exploring the development of algorithms that can generalize from previous experience-is now complete.

item.title: Learning policy representations in multiagent systems
Improving language understanding with unsupervised learning
item.description: We've obtained state-of-the-art results on a suite of diverse language tasks with a scalable, task-agnostic system, which we're also releasing. Our approach is a combination of two existing ideas: transformers and unsupervised pre-training. These results provide a convincing example that pairing supervised learning methods with unsupervised pre-training works very well; this is an idea that many have explored in the past, and we hope our result motivates further research into applying this idea on larger and more diverse datasets.

item.title: GamePad: A learning environment for theorem proving
OpenAI Fellows Fall 2018 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has announced the opening of applications for its Fall 2018 Fellows program, which provides a paid six-month apprenticeship in artificial intelligence research at OpenAI.

item.title: Gym Retro
item.description: We're releasing the full version of Gym Retro, a platform for reinforcement learning research on games. This brings our publicly-released game count from around 70 Atari games and 30 Sega games to over 1,000 games across a variety of backing emulators. We're also releasing the tool we use to add new games to the platform.

item.title: AI and compute
item.description: We're releasing an analysis showing that since 2012, the amount of compute used in the largest AI training runs has been increasing exponentially with a 3.4-month doubling time (by comparison, Moore's Law had a 2-year doubling period)[^footnote-correction]. Since 2012, this metric has grown by more than 300,000x (a 2-year doubling period would yield only a 7x increase). Improvements in compute have been a key component of AI progress, so as long as this trend continues, it's worth preparing for the implications of systems far outside today's capabilities.

item.title: AI safety via debate
item.description: We're proposing an AI safety technique which trains agents to debate topics with one another, using a human to judge who wins.

item.title: Evolved Policy Gradients
item.description: We're releasing an experimental metalearning approach called Evolved Policy Gradients, a method that evolves the loss function of learning agents, which can enable fast training on novel tasks. Agents trained with EPG can succeed at basic tasks at test time that were outside their training regime, like learning to navigate to an object on a different side of the room from where it was placed during training.

item.title: Gotta Learn Fast: A new benchmark for generalization in RL
Retro Contest
item.description: We're launching a transfer learning contest that measures a reinforcement learning algorithm's ability to generalize from previous experience.

item.title: Variance reduction for policy gradient with action-dependent factorized baselines
Improving GANs using optimal transport
Report from the OpenAI hackathon
item.description: On March 3rd, we hosted our first hackathon with 100 members of the artificial intelligence community.

item.title: On first-order meta-learning algorithms
Reptile: A scalable meta-learning algorithm
item.description: We've developed a simple meta-learning algorithm called Reptile which works by repeatedly sampling a task, performing stochastic gradient descent on it, and updating the initial parameters towards the final parameters learned on that task. Reptile is the application of the Shortest Descent algorithm to the meta-learning setting, and is mathematically similar to first-order MAML (which is a version of the well-known MAML algorithm) that only needs black-box access to an optimizer such as SGD or Adam, with similar computational efficiency and performance.

item.title: OpenAI Scholars
item.description: We're providing 6-10 stipends and mentorship to individuals from underrepresented groups to study deep learning full-time for 3 months and open-source a project.

item.title: Some considerations on learning to explore via meta-reinforcement learning
Multi-Goal Reinforcement Learning: Challenging robotics environments and request for research
Ingredients for robotics research
item.description: We're releasing eight simulated robotics environments and a Baselines implementation of Hindsight Experience Replay, all developed for our research over the past year. We've used these environments to train models which work on physical robots. We're also releasing a set of requests for robotics research.

item.title: OpenAI hackathon
item.description: Come to OpenAI's office in San Francisco's Mission District for talks and a hackathon on Saturday, March 3rd.

item.title: OpenAI supporters
item.description: We're excited to welcome new donors to OpenAI.

item.title: Preparing for malicious uses of AI
item.description: We've co-authored a paper that forecasts how malicious actors could misuse AI technology, and potential ways we can prevent and mitigate these threats. This paper is the outcome of almost a year of sustained work with our colleagues at the Future of Humanity Institute, the Centre for the Study of Existential Risk, the Center for a New American Security, the Electronic Frontier Foundation, and others.

item.title: Interpretable machine learning through teaching
item.description: We've designed a method that encourages AIs to teach each other with examples that also make sense to humans. Our approach automatically selects the most informative examples to teach a concept-for instance, the best images to describe the concept of dogs-and experimentally we found our approach to be effective at teaching both AIs

item.title: Discovering types for entity disambiguation
item.description: We've built a system for automatically figuring out which object is meant by a word by having a neural network decide if the word belongs to each of about 100 automatically-discovered "types" (non-exclusive categories).

item.title: Requests for Research 2.0 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: OpenAI has announced the release of seven new unsolved research problems identified during their ongoing work. These challenges aim to guide and inspire further investigation in the field of artificial intelligence.

item.title: Scaling Kubernetes to 2,500 nodes
Block-sparse GPU kernels
item.description: We're releasing highly-optimized GPU kernels for an underexplored class of neural network architectures: networks with block-sparse weights. Depending on the chosen sparsity, these kernels can run orders of magnitude faster than cuBLAS or cuSPARSE. We've used them to attain state-of-the-art results in text sentiment analysis and generative modeling of text and images.

item.title: Learning sparse neural networks through L0 regularization
Interpretable and pedagogical examples
Learning a hierarchy
item.description: We've developed a hierarchical reinforcement learning algorithm that learns high-level actions useful for solving a range of tasks, allowing fast solving of tasks requiring thousands of timesteps. Our algorithm, when applied to a set of navigation problems, discovers a set of high-level actions for walking and crawling in different directions, which enables the agent to master new navigation tasks quickly.

item.title: Generalizing from simulation
item.description: Our latest robotics techniques allow robot controllers, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on physical robots, to react to unplanned changes in the environment as they solve simple tasks. That is, we've used these techniques to build closed-loop systems rather than open-loop ones as before.

item.title: Asymmetric actor critic for image-based robot learning
Sim-to-real transfer of robotic control with dynamics randomization
Domain randomization and generative models for robotic grasping
Meta-learning for wrestling
item.description: We show that for the task of simulated robot wrestling, a meta-learning agent can learn to quickly defeat a stronger non-meta-learning agent, and also show that the meta-learning agent can adapt to physical malfunction.

item.title: Competitive self-play
item.description: We've found that self-play allows simulated AIs to discover physical skills like tackling, ducking, faking, kicking, catching, and diving for the ball, without explicitly designing an environment with these skills in mind. Self-play ensures that the environment is always the right difficulty for an AI to improve. Taken alongside our Dota 2 self-play results, we have increasing confidence that self-play will be a core part of powerful AI systems in the future.

item.title: Nonlinear computation in deep linear networks
Learning to model other minds
item.description: We're releasing an algorithm which accounts for the fact that other agents are learning too, and discovers self-interested yet collaborative strategies like tit-for-tat in the iterated prisoner's dilemma. This algorithm, Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness (LOLA), is a small step towards agents that model other minds.

item.title: Learning with opponent-learning awareness
OpenAI Baselines: ACKTR & A2C
item.description: We're releasing two new OpenAI Baselines implementations: ACKTR and A2C. A2C is a synchronous, deterministic variant of Asynchronous Advantage Actor Critic (A3C) which we've found gives equal performance. ACKTR is a more sample-efficient reinforcement learning algorithm than TRPO and A2C, and requires only slightly more computation than A2C per update.

item.title: More on Dota 2
item.description: Our Dota 2 result shows that self-play can catapult the performance of machine learning systems from far below human level to superhuman, given sufficient compute. In the span of a month, our system went from barely matching a high-ranked player to beating the top pros and has continued to improve since then. Supervised deep learning systems can only be as good as their training datasets, but in self-play systems, the available data improves automatically as the agent gets better.

item.title: Dota 2
item.description: We've created a bot which beats the world's top professionals at 1v1 matches of Dota 2 under standard tournament rules. The bot learned the game from scratch by self-play, and does not use imitation learning or tree search. This is a step towards building AI systems which accomplish well-defined goals in messy, complicated situations involving real humans.

item.title: Gathering human feedback
item.description: RL-Teacher is an open-source implementation of our interface to train AIs via occasional human feedback rather than hand-crafted reward functions. The underlying technique was developed as a step towards safe AI systems, but also applies to reinforcement learning problems with rewards that are hard to specify.

item.title: Better exploration with parameter noise
item.description: We've found that adding adaptive noise to the parameters of reinforcement learning algorithms frequently boosts performance. This exploration method is simple to implement and very rarely decreases performance, so it's worth trying on any problem.

item.title: Proximal Policy Optimization
item.description: We're releasing a new class of reinforcement learning algorithms, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which perform comparably or better than state-of-the-art approaches while being much simpler to implement and tune. PPO has become the default reinforcement learning algorithm at OpenAI because of its ease of use and good performance.

item.title: Robust adversarial inputs
item.description: We've created images that reliably fool neural network classifiers when viewed from varied scales and perspectives. This challenges a claim from last week that self-driving cars would be hard to trick maliciously since they capture images from multiple scales, angles, perspectives, and the like.

item.title: Hindsight Experience Replay
Teacher-student curriculum learning
Faster physics in Python
item.description: A new high-performance Python library for robotic simulation, utilizing the MuJoCo engine, has been open-sourced. This library was developed over the past year as part of robotics research efforts.

item.title: Learning from human preferences
item.description: One step towards building safe AI systems is to remove the need for humans to write goal functions, since using a simple proxy for a complex goal, or getting the complex goal a bit wrong, can lead to undesirable and even dangerous behavior. In collaboration with DeepMind's safety team, we've developed an algorithm which can infer what humans want by being told which of two proposed behaviors is better.

item.title: Learning to cooperate, compete, and communicate
item.description: Multiagent environments where agents compete for resources are stepping stones on the path to AGI. Multiagent environments have two useful properties: first, there is a natural curriculum-the difficulty of the environment is determined by the skill of your competitors (and if you're competing against clones of yourself, the environment exactly matches your skill level). Second, a multiagent environment has no stable equilibrium: no matter how smart an agent is, there's always pressure to get smarter. These environments have a very different feel from traditional environments, and it'll take a lot more research before we become good at them.

item.title: UCB exploration via Q-ensembles
OpenAI Baselines: DQN [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: We're open-sourcing OpenAI Baselines, our internal effort to reproduce reinforcement learning algorithms with performance on par with published results. We'll release the algorithms over upcoming months; today's release includes DQN and three of its variants.

item.title: Robots that learn
item.description: We've created a robotics system, trained entirely in simulation and deployed on a physical robot, which can learn a new task after seeing it done once.

item.title: Roboschool
item.description: We are releasing Roboschool: open-source software for robot simulation, integrated with OpenAI Gym.

item.title: Equivalence between policy gradients and soft Q-learning
Stochastic Neural Networks for hierarchical reinforcement learning
Unsupervised sentiment neuron
item.description: We've developed an unsupervised system which learns an excellent representation of sentiment, despite being trained only to predict the next character in the text of Amazon reviews.

item.title: Spam detection in the physical world
item.description: We've created the world's first Spam-detecting AI trained entirely in simulation and deployed on a physical robot.

item.title: Evolution strategies as a scalable alternative to reinforcement learning
item.description: We've discovered that evolution strategies (ES), an optimization technique that's been known for decades, rivals the performance of standard reinforcement learning (RL) techniques on modern RL benchmarks (e.g. Atari/MuJoCo), while overcoming many of RL's inconveniences.

item.title: One-shot imitation learning
Distill
item.description: We're excited to support today's launch of Distill, a new kind of journal aimed at excellent communication of machine learning results (novel or existing).

item.title: Learning to communicate
item.description: In this post we'll outline new OpenAI research in which agents develop their own language.

item.title: Emergence of grounded compositional language in multi-agent populations
Prediction and control with temporal segment models
Third-person imitation learning
Attacking machine learning with adversarial examples
item.description: Adversarial examples are inputs to machine learning models that an attacker has intentionally designed to cause the model to make a mistake; they're like optical illusions for machines. In this post we'll show how adversarial examples work across different mediums, and will discuss why securing systems against them can be difficult.

item.title: Adversarial attacks on neural network policies
Team update
item.description: The OpenAI team is now 45 people. Together, we're pushing the frontier of AI capabilities-whether by validating novel ideas, creating new software systems, or deploying machine learning on robots.

item.title: PixelCNN++: Improving the PixelCNN with discretized logistic mixture likelihood and other modifications
Faulty reward functions in the wild
item.description: Reinforcement learning algorithms can break in surprising, counterintuitive ways. In this post we'll explore one failure mode, which is where you misspecify your reward function.

item.title: Universe
item.description: We're releasing Universe, a software platform for measuring and training an AI's general intelligence across the world's supply of games, websites and other applications.

item.title: #Exploration: A study of count-based exploration for deep reinforcement learning
OpenAI and Microsoft
item.description: We're working with Microsoft to start running most of our large-scale experiments on Azure.

item.title: On the quantitative analysis of decoder-based generative models
A connection between generative adversarial networks, inverse reinforcement learning, and energy-based models
RL2: Fast reinforcement learning via slow reinforcement learning
Variational lossy autoencoder
Extensions and limitations of the neural GPU
Semi-supervised knowledge transfer for deep learning from private training data
Report from the self-organizing conference
item.description: Last week we hosted over a hundred and fifty AI practitioners in our offices for our first self-organizing conference on machine learning.

item.title: Transfer from simulation to real world through learning deep inverse dynamics model
Infrastructure for deep learning
item.description: Deep learning is an empirical science, and the quality of a group's infrastructure is a multiplier on progress. Fortunately, today's open-source ecosystem makes it possible for anyone to build great deep learning infrastructure.
